'the accusation lands' is shots.json's own wording and is left verbatim; the accuser is established one line earlier (line 64/65 put Kamata at the desk with the ledger) and named again on line 68 ('told so by the uncle who reads your ledgers better than you do'). B73 says only 'Kamata tells him his own partner has been stealing from the operation', and shots.json clip:01:07:29 records only that 'he drops his eyes'. Dropped eyes in front of the head of the yakuza read at least as well as shame or submission as they do as surprise, and the transcript carries no English line for Kamata's accusation at all (01:07:29; the nearest intelligible segments are [482] 'Your...' at 01:07:23 and [486] 'The horse can't run because of the lack of iron' at 01:08:00, which is B74's proverb). Nothing factual was removed: the setting, the accusation, Han's name, his partner/front role, the money, the books, the non-denial and the lowered eyes all survive. Landed 32 words against a 35 budget, three under, which buys real audio margin (40 words = 23.04s, so ~0.58s/word puts 32 words near 18.4s against an 18.9s budget; 35 words would have been ~20.2s and still long).

audit.fact: Every surviving claim traces to a source. Setting + accusation + lowered eyes: shots.json clip:01:07:29, which is this line's exact window (01:07:29.823-01:07:46.090). The accusation's content: B73 (beats_proposal.md:86) and reveals.json R1 ('Han has been stealing from the Yakuza operation he fronts for'). Han as Takashi's partner: film_facts.json ('DK's business partner') plus names.json (Takashi = DK, both Brian Tee). Non-denial: shots.json clip:01:07:46, 'standing stiff and silent, offering nothing back'. The one claim that was NOT traceable - 'he didn't know either' - is the one I removed.
audit.fact_loss: none. The removed clause was interpretation, so nothing factual left the script. The nearest real idea it gestured at - that Takashi is being told something about his own operation he could not see himself - survives in attributed form on line 68, 'told so by the uncle who reads your ledgers better than you do'. Han's partner role, which line 68 depends on ('Robbed by your own partner'), is still named here and nowhere else in the B72-B75 run.
audit.invention: none. Pure subtraction: every word of the output appears in the input, in the same order. No name, role, term or causal link was added, and the shorter text asserts strictly less than the longer one - it now stops at what the camera shows.
audit.spoiler: ok. R1 lands at 01:07:29, the first frame of this line's window, so naming the skim here is on-time rather than early. No R2 term appears (no 'dies', 'killed', 'last', 'won't make it'); the line does not touch Han's fate, and the next beat in the script is B75, the garage, not the crash. No R3 term ('new DK', 'runs the mountain') and no R4 term ('Toretto', 'family', 'from the earlier films'). 'the books' is B72's own wording ('go through the books') and is not R1's held phrase 'cooking the books'.

lines.dropped: One word, the evaluative adjective in 'the good car' -> 'his car'. 'Good' was the narrator's ranking of Han's car against the Evo he had already given Sean, and nothing in B57 or the transcript grades the cars; what the transcript does say is 'your car' (segment [390]), i.e. Han's own, which 'his car' states directly. So the substitution is a word shorter and closer to the source than what it replaced. The referent is unambiguous: 'his' sits inside 'why Han never let him race...', with Han as the subject of 'let', and Sean's own car is the red Evo he has been racing for ten minutes of screen time.

audit.fact: Both halves verified in the transcript. Question: [390] 00:51:37.9 'Why didn't you let me race with your car?' Answer: [397] 00:52:01.7 'One car in exchange for knowing what a man's made of' and [398] 00:52:05.7 'That's a prize I can live with.' B57 (beats_proposal.md:70) confirms the speaker and the deliberateness: 'the long-haired man ... admits he lent out the car on purpose: one car in exchange for knowing what a man is made of is a prize he can live with'. PRIZE/PRICE: the word is PRIZE, confirmed verbatim at [398], and the trimmed line does not use either word, so the inversion cannot be re-introduced from here. Line 49, the next line, already carries it correctly - 'is a prize he can live with' - so the script's standing text is now right and this trim leaves it right. Marginal, carried over from the pre-trim line and not introduced by me: 'what the kid was made of' narrows Han's general 'what a man's made of' to Sean. I kept it rather than switching to 'a man' on purpose - line 49 restores Han's generalisation in full, and making line 48 say 'a man' too would have had the VO speak nearly the same clause twice in a row.
audit.fact_loss: none. Nothing in the script elsewhere depended on Han's car being called 'good'; line 44 already establishes the car hierarchy from the other direction ('Han won't let his name roll around Tokyo in a Hyundai'), and lines 43-44 establish that the car Sean does have is the red Evo Han handed him. Ownership of the withheld car is now stated more plainly than before.
audit.invention: none. The shorter text asserts less, not more: an unsupported quality judgement ('good') is replaced by a transcript-supported possessive ('his'). No new name, number, motive or causal link.
audit.spoiler: ok. B57 is at 00:51:21, long before every reveal: R1 lands 01:07:29, R2 01:15:07, R3 01:33:41, R4 01:36:38. The line says nothing about the skim, the crash, the mountain or the cameo. It is R4 *setup* per angle.md ('R4 setup: B57 (Han's own story)'), which is setup, not disclosure - and the trim removed nothing that setup needs.
